name: Nokia SR Linux Container Image
what_it_is: Nokia Service Router Linux (SR Linux) is a fully open network operating system (NOS) distributed as a free container image (ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux) with no registration, licensing, or contract requirements. It is intended for learning, demo, test, and CI environments — not production deployment.
components: SR Linux NOS (network operating system) packaged as a container image
Nokia Data Center Fabric control plane (BGP, EVPN, IS-IS, OSPF, VXLAN)
measurement: gNMI streaming telemetry for operational state and counters
configuration: JSON-RPC API for configuration and state queries
CLI over SSH for interactive configuration
modes: Containerized lab/test mode (learning, demo, CI) — the only documented use case for this image
Topology node in multi-container labs (e.g., via Containerlab)
constraints: Explicitly not intended for production deployment — image is scoped to learning, demo, test, and CI environments only
No licensing or registration required, but this also means no Nokia support SLA for the container image distribution
Requires Linux host with Docker; container runs as a privileged/network-capable container due to NOS kernel requirements
Latest release at time of research is 26.3.1 — versioning follows Nokia SR Linux software release cadence
docker_services: ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux — single container image; no docker-compose.yml is included in the repository (the repo is purely a distribution and release-notes vehicle)
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the repository — users must compose their own topology files or use Containerlab
No fault injection or traffic generation tooling bundled in this image
No production licensing or support pathway via this container image distribution
No CI/test harness scripts in the repository (only release automation scripts: add-release.sh, publi.sh)
